title: The Quench-Slurry Ratio
story: High on the volcano road, Thrumbrask the Slag Piper blows molten slag down the switchbacks, and the cart drivers are stranded behind a glowing river. The old quench-masters say only slurry mixed in exactly 5 parts cinder-ash to 3 parts springwater will cool it, and Mr 6 has one barrel that holds 48 gallons of slurry. He rolls up his cape and picks up the measuring ladle.
question: If Mr 6 fills all 48 gallons in a 5:3 ratio of cinder-ash to springwater, how many gallons of springwater does he pour in?
solution: The mix has 5 + 3 = 8 equal parts in all.
praise: Thinking in parts was exactly the right move — the one missing step was multiplying a single part by the 3 water parts.
hint: Add the two ratio numbers first: how many equal parts make up the whole 48 gallons?
victory: The slurry hits the slag with a hiss, and the glowing river freezes into a harmless gray road. Thrumbrask puffs one sulky smoke ring and pipes himself back down the crater, muttering about arithmetic.
imagePrompt: A brave numeral-six knight in a blue cape tipping a huge barrel of silver slurry onto a glowing orange slag river while a lanky ash-colored piper monster recoils in a smoky volcanic pass at dusk.
